contract.pre_condition: vaddr is page-aligned by type and denotes an eligible user virtual page for vmem: it is within the valid user range and is not a protected, kernel, or shared mapping that this operation lacks authority to remove. vmem's page-table representation, abstract mapping relation, and ownership capabilities are coherent. If active-address-space identity is part of the intended behavior, either vmem is the selected active address space or Vmem::unmap is explicitly permitted to modify an inactive one. The wrapper additionally requires Vmem::unmap and UserFrame destruction to satisfy the obligations below; the body itself does not validate these conditions.
contract.post_condition: On Ok(true), Vmem::unmap returned Ok(Some(frame)); this body consumed that option and dropped frame before returning. Subject to the callee and destructor contracts, the selected abstract mapping is absent, every unrelated mapping and preserved identity is unchanged, and authority for the removed backing user frame is released or transferred exactly once. On Ok(false), Vmem::unmap returned Ok(None); subject to its contract, the abstract mapping relation is unchanged. Cleanup or reclamation of an empty lower-level page table may change hidden representation in either successful case only when its ownership and emptiness preconditions hold, and must not change the abstract mapping result.
contract.failure_condition: If Vmem::unmap returns Err(e), this body returns Err(e), never converts it into successful removal, and performs no later explicit mutation or frame release. The body alone cannot establish failure atomicity: Vmem::unmap may already have partially mutated page-table representation, cleanup state, mappings, or ownership before returning Err. The minimum safe failure contract must state either that all observable abstract state is unchanged or precisely which partial concrete mutations may remain, while forbidding an unreported removed mapping or lost/duplicated frame authority.

abstraction.name: Selected-user-page mapping with representation and ownership separation

abstract_state.user_mapping: M: eligible user virtual pages -> optional backing user-frame identities and abstract permissions.
abstract_state.page_table_representation: R: page-directory and lower-level page-table objects, entries, flags, links, and allocation metadata that encode M.
abstract_state.backing_frame_authority: A: ownership or allocator capabilities for mapped user frames, temporarily returned UserFrame values, and free frames.
abstract_state.cleanup_state: C: lower-level table occupancy, cleanup eligibility, ownership, pending reclamation, and reclaimed-table status.
abstract_state.identity_state: I: active address-space identity, vmem identity, allocator identity, and protected/kernel/shared mapping identities.

abstraction.projection: project(R) = M for eligible user mappings. A present eligible leaf entry for virtual page v projects to M[v] = frame(entry) with its abstract permissions; absence projects to M[v] = none. Empty intermediate tables and their presence or reclamation are representation details and do not independently contribute mappings.
abstraction.preserved_state: For selected page v, all M[u] with u != v are preserved. Active address-space identity, vmem identity, allocator identity, protected/kernel/shared mappings, and authority unrelated to the selected mapping are preserved. Reclamation may alter R and C only for an empty lower-level table made or found reclaimable under valid ownership; it must preserve project(R) except for removal of M[v] when a mapping existed.
abstraction.hidden_representation: Page-table allocation layout, directory/table indices, empty-but-allocated lower-level tables, entry encoding, TLB maintenance mechanism, cleanup ordering, and the concrete allocator bookkeeping used to reclaim a table or backing frame are hidden provided their future observable behavior refines M, A, C, and I.
abstraction.observation_boundary: The operation is observed after the complete Rust call expression, including evaluation of is_some(), destruction of any returned UserFrame, and construction of Result<bool, Error>. Observable effects are the returned result, the post-call abstract mapping relation through future address translation or Vmem operations, preserved identities and mappings, and allocator-visible authority or later frame reuse. Intermediate page-table states are outside the boundary only if they cannot be observed concurrently, through faults, panics, callbacks, or missing synchronization.

obligations.title: Result-to-mapping correspondence
obligations.claim: For eligible v, Vmem::unmap(v) returns Ok(Some(f)) if and only if the pre-state M maps v to f, and then the post-state mapping is exactly the pre-state mapping with v removed. It returns Ok(None) if and only if v was absent, and then the mapping relation is unchanged.
obligations.why_blocking: This is the minimum fact needed for the wrapper's boolean to describe abstract removal rather than merely the callee's option tag.

obligations.title: Mapping frame condition
obligations.claim: Vmem::unmap preserves every abstract mapping other than the eligible selected user page, including protected, kernel, and shared mappings.
obligations.why_blocking: The wrapper contains no checks or restoration logic, so all mapping noninterference depends on the callee.

suggested_callees.reason: Prove that traversal, leaf mutation, and cleanup are confined to the selected mapping and permitted representation objects.

obligations.title: Returned-frame authority
obligations.claim: On Ok(Some(f)), Vmem::unmap transfers exactly one valid owning UserFrame capability for the formerly mapped backing frame, removes the corresponding mapping authority, and retains no second owning capability that can release the same frame.
obligations.why_blocking: The wrapper immediately drops the value; incorrect provenance or duplicated authority could leak, double-release, or release a still-mapped frame.

candidate_variants.name: Stronger failure-atomic and synchronous-release contract
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Every Err preserves M, reachable representation semantics, A, C, and I exactly, while Ok(true) completes translation invalidation and physical-frame release before return.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Inject failure after clearing the selected leaf but before cleanup or frame construction. This variant permits only restoration followed by Err; an absent mapping, stale translation, or unreleased frame authority violates it.

candidate_variants.name: Minimum caller-facing abstract contract
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Requires exact Some or None correspondence to selected abstract mapping removal, preservation of unrelated abstract mappings and identities, and unique returned-frame authority. It allows representation-only cleanup and documented partial concrete mutation on Err if projected mappings and ownership remain safe.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Begin with the selected page unmapped but an empty allocated lower-level table present. Returning Ok(false) after reclaiming that table satisfies this variant because M is unchanged, but violates a representation-preserving contract.

candidate_variants.name: Weaker option-tag contract
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Promises only that Ok(true), Ok(false), and Err correspond to Ok(Some(_)), Ok(None), and Err from Vmem::unmap, and that Rust drops any Some payload. It makes no claim about mapping removal, framing, cleanup, or allocator effects.
candidate_variants.discriminator: A Vmem::unmap implementation that returns Ok(Some(frame)) without deleting the selected mapping satisfies this weak wrapper contract and yields Ok(true), but violates the selected-page unmap intent.

candidate_variants.name: Deferred-release ownership contract
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Requires unique authority to leave the mapping exactly once but permits UserFrame destruction to enqueue or transfer release rather than making the physical frame immediately reusable before return.
candidate_variants.discriminator: After Ok(true), query the allocator immediately. A quarantined frame that becomes reusable only after deferred reclamation satisfies this variant but violates the synchronous-release variant.
